title: Co-development of a web-app for young people with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
official: Protocol for co-development, initial evaluation, and implementation of a digital health intervention, for young people (aged 16-30 years) with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, including optimisation for sustainable delivery via health and social care settings
summary:
Background and study aims
Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a condition that affects how people think, process information, and interact with others. It is characterized by challenges with attention, focus, restlessness, and/or impulsivity.
For young people aged 16-30 years, managing their ADHD can be particularly difficult. They are at increased risk of mental health crises and other challenges. Treatment and support can reduce these risks, with benefits for individuals and society.
However, many young people with ADHD struggle to get the healthcare they need during this vulnerable time. Facing long waiting times, or gaps in support between child and adult services. Digital interventions could help improve access to care.
This project aims to co-develop and test an app to help improve access to care. The app will provide trusted healthcare information, psychological support, and practical tools to help young people manage their daily lives and ADHD symptoms.

Who can participate?
Young people aged 16-30 years with a diagnosis of ADHD or on the waiting list for an ADHD assessment.
Young people will need to be able to test the prototype on their own or with help from a supporter.
Healthcare professionals working in the NHS, with experience of supporting people with ADHD or suspected ADHD

What does the study involve?
Young people who are participants will be invited to take part in a workshop to try out a prototype of the app. The workshops will take place in person or online. Participants will be asked questions about using the app and asked to give feedback on how to improve it and make it more useful for young people living in the ADHD. Participants will also be asked how well this app might work in the NHS. After the workshops have finished, participants may be invited to a follow-up interview about their experiences of using the app.
Healthcare professionals who are participants will be invited to take part in an interview or focus group, where they will be invited to view a prototype of the app. Then they will be asked to answer questions about the app and ways it could be embedded into NHS care pathways. These activities will take place in person or online (depending on the preferences of participants).

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
By taking part, participants will help the research team to gather valuable information to help improve the design of the SmartADHD app. Helping to meet our long-term aim of improving the lives of young people with ADHD and making it easier for healthcare professionals to support them.
Young people and healthcare professionals will be offered a voucher, as a thank you for participating in the research and contributing their time, energy and expertise. Healthcare professionals will be provided with a continuing professional development certificate.

Where is the study run from?
The SmartADHD study is being run by the University of Exeter.
Work package one (WP1) will be conducted from the University of Exeter, with workshops taking place in a range of community settings (in-person or online).
Work package two (WP2) will be conducted from the University of Exeter, with some participants being recruited from primary care practices across the UK.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
September 2026 to March 2029

Who is funding the study?
The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Associate Professor Anna Price: a.price@exeter.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Eligible participants will be young people aged 16-30 years with an ADHD diagnosis or awaiting assessment (WP1 and WP2) and healthcare professionals involved in delivering healthcare to people with ADHD (WP2 only).

Young people (WP1 and WP2):
1. One of the following
1.1. A person aged 16 to 30 years diagnosed with ADHD, or
1.2. A person aged 16 to 30 years who have been referred for an assessment for ADHD
2. Able to engage in a test of the prototype and communicate their experience, either
2.1. Independently or
2.2. With a supporter
3. Resident, working, or studying in the UK

Additional criteria (WP2 only):
4. Registered with a GP or an NHS service for people with ADHD

Healthcare professionals (WP2 only):
1. Healthcare professional (involved in NHS care, including clinical, managerial, leadership and administrative roles)
2. Has experience of supporting patients with ADHD or suspected ADHD
3. Resident or working in the UK
Exclusion criteria:
Young people (WP1 and WP2):
1. Not a person aged 16 to 30 years with a diagnosis of or awaiting assessment for ADHD 
2. Not resident, working, or studying in the UK
3. Not able to engage in a test of the prototype, independently, or with help from a supporter

Healthcare professionals (WP2 only):
1. Not a healthcare professional 
2. Does not have experience of supporting patients with ADHD or suspected ADHD
3. Not resident or working in the UK
